correctness.rationale: The projected orbit is exactly the forward orbit of 0 in the finite ring. For gcd(m,6)=1, the inverse of the permutation BA is a power of BA, so AB(BA)^{-1} is a permitted forward transformation and translates by 2, a generator of the additive residue group. This includes the trivial ring m=1. If 3 does not divide m, representatives for the even and odd halves of Z/(2m) come from A and C respectively, using that 3 is a unit modulo m for the odd half. If 2 does not divide m, C, AB and B produce the three residue classes mod 3 in Z/(3m), using invertibility of 2 modulo m in the first two. Factoring out a power of 2 or 3 exhausts the moduli not divisible by 6. Neither the seed nor any generator output is 1 modulo 6, so every multiple of 6 misses a class. All prime powers therefore have full support, whereas the cylinder 1 mod 6 is disjoint from the orbit in the profinite completion.
residual_risks: The packaged BFS constructs exact reachable sets for a finite range only and was not run in this review. No universal computation is needed.
The theorem is not an exact residue-count formula for every mixed modulus or a claim about ordinary counting density.

value.rationale: The orbit is a named, previously studied critical Klarner example. The classification identifies exactly when congruences give an obstruction, including the failure of simultaneous 2- and 3-adic support despite full support in either coordinate separately. This distinguishes ordinary density questions from the exact local/profinite obstruction and is useful independently of finer mixed-prime counts.
residual_risks: No ordinary counting-density conclusion follows; exact mixed-prime image descriptions need separate results.
